Sarah (Sales): FYI EpochAI POC - customers seeing slow TTFT and intermittent 429s during bursts. Also reporting a 403-looking auth message when we switch to their VPC private endpoint. They asked about Dedicated pricing for a short demo. Can we swarm?
Mateo (Solutions): can you paste the exact error and a sample request-id? also what model + seq len + concurrent clients?
Sarah (Sales): error from their logs: "ERROR authz: 403 policy denied egress to model.redwood.internal for token tk_***". sample request id they sent: req_42ab7f. Model: rw-instruct-small-ish (pinned), seq ~1024 typical, bursts ~60 rps across ~8 parallel clients.
Priya (SRE): 2 quick things: 1) 429s during burst = likely token-bucket or internal concurrency throttle. check response headers for X-Redwood-Quota and X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining on failing requests. 2) small client batch windows + many clients => lots of tiny batches, killing throughput/TTFT. Can you confirm client batching settings?
Jing (Eng Oncall): + we saw high KV cache miss rate for that model on the recent host — cache.hit_rate ~0.12 in last 10m which increases token work and TTFT. Also: the auth error looks like an IAM policy denying egress to the private model endpoint when requests originate from their VPC connector. Need their VPC/NAT + our egress allowlist details.
Sarah (Sales): client is using default SDK settings, looks like batching set to 5ms. They said they tried streaming off but same issue. Jess (from customer) attached a trace link but I don't have console access to view.
Mateo (Solutions): ask them to set client.batch_window_ms = 20-30ms (this reduces tiny batches) and try enabling shared_prefix_cache = true for the session. For quick mitigation, reduce concurrent clients from 8 -> 4 to smooth the token-bucket. If still 429s we can route to Dedicated pool fallback.
Carlos (Security): on the VPC/auth side: if they want Private, we need the security questionnaire answers about KMS requirements and allowed CIDR blocks. Also confirm whether they require customer-managed keys (HSM) — that changes onboarding timeline. Sarah, can you get the SQ doc?
Emma (Customer Success): I can run the calendar invite for a 30m swarm with EpochAI. Recommend we offer a short Dedicated trial (2 weeks, single GPU pool) to demonstrate stable TTFT; legal can do a temporary addendum. I don't want sales to promise credits without ops signoff though.
deploy-bot: New deploy to prod: runtime v2.14.1 — no config changes to batching.
Jing (Eng Oncall): collect these before the call: - full failing request header (X-Request-ID) - response headers (X-Redwood-Quota, X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining, X-Redwood-Host) - a short repro payload (system + user prompt) - trace link or curl to our traces API: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \ 
  https://console.redwood.dev/api/traces/req_42ab7f```
Priya (SRE): also run a quick internal check: ```rbxctl metrics query --range 10m "model.kv_cache.hit_rate{model=\"rw-instruct-small-ish\"}"``` if hit_rate < 0.3 we should enable shared cache and bump cache warmup.
Sarah (Sales): thanks all — I'll grab the SQ and failing headers from EpochAI and schedule the swarm for tomorrow 10:00 PST. I'll also ask them to flip batch_window to 25ms for a quick test and send results. :thumbsup:
Mateo (Solutions): if they send the trace link I can annotate where the tiny batches are happening and propose client-side patch. If those changes don't help we can prep a Dedicated fallback and a cost estimate for Emma to share.
Sarah (Sales): queued to send docs + headers later today, will follow up here after the call.
notes: short thread, coordinating POC swarm: authz/VPC, 429s, batching, cache hit rate, short Dedicated trial/pricing question
